2009 USBWA Second Team All-American }} '''Lucas Cameron "Luke" Harangody''' (born January 2, 1988 in [[Decatur, Illinois]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who completed his [[college basketball|college]] career at the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|University of Notre Dame]] in [[2009–10 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|2010]]. A [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]], Harangody is the only men's player in the history of the [[Big East Conference]] to average 20 points and 10 rebounds per game in conference play for his career.{{cite press release|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030710aab.html |title=Luke Harangody And Tim Abromaitis Garner All-BIG EAST Conference Honors |publisher=University of Notre Dame |date=2010-03-07 |accessdate=2010-03-18}} He was also the 2008 [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]],{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/wires/03/11/2060.ap.bkc.big.east.awards.0300/|title=Notre Dame's Harangody and Brey sweep Big East postseason awards|publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]''|date=2008-03-11|accessdate=2008-10-13}} and was also named to the second team on the 2008 [[Associated Press]] [[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]] team.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=3322266 ESPN – For first time in six decades, no seniors on AP All-America team – Men's College Basketball] He is also the first Notre Dame men's player to be a three-time first-team All-Big East selection (2008–2010), and the first men's player to lead the conference in both scoring and rebounding in consecutive seasons (2008 and 2009). Harangody considered entering the 2009 NBA Draft, but withdrew his name to return to Notre Dame for his senior season. http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2009/06/20/2009-06-20_luke_harangody_withdraws.html ==Early years== Growing up in [[Schererville, Indiana]], Harangody, the son of a former [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana University football]] player, had an intense [[sibling rivalry]] with his brother Ty, who is 20 months older and was one grade ahead of him in school. The two began with basketball games on a mini-hoop in Harangody's room, which ended when they were kicked out for shaking the light fixtures. The games then moved to a court that their father set up in the basement, and from there to the backyard once they outgrew the basement. Their father soon banned them from the backyard because their one-on-one games almost invariably ended in fistfights, but that only moved their rivalry to local parks. Bigger and stronger, Ty won most of their games; Harangody would later say about those days, "I still look back on that as where most of my competitive nature comes from. To beat him, I'd go all out, all the time." Eventually, the brothers' athletic paths split. Ty followed in their father's footsteps as a football player, eventually earning a [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] to IU as a [[tight end]]; his career was ended by a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his sophomore year. Harangody grew 3 inches as a high school freshman and opted for basketball.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?id=3254631 |title= Harangody emerging as Big East's best big man |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]'' |date=2008-02-27 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} Harangody starred at [[Andrean High School]] in nearby [[Merrillville, Indiana|Merrillville]]. In his last two high school seasons, he averaged over 20 points and 10 rebounds, was named as the top player in Northwest Indiana by at least one media outlet in each season, and received All-State recognition in Indiana in both seasons.{{cite web|url=http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harangody_luke00.html |title=Men's Basketball Player Bio: Luke Harangody |publisher=University of Notre Dame Athletic Department |accessdate=2008-10-13}} ==Collegiate career== ===Freshman season=== Despite Harangody's credentials, he had considerable doubts about his ability to play in the [[Big East Conference|Big East]], and much of [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame's]] recruitment consisted of convincing him he was good enough to play in the conference. During preseason practices, he remembered being "absolutely destroyed" by teammate Rob Kurz. After most practices, he called his father, who remembers Luke telling him "I will never see the court, I will always be a bench player", he screamed in agony. Those doubts would start to disappear shortly after the season started, when he scored in double figures in five straight games. After a [[double-double]] against [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] in the second game of the season, Irish head coach [[Mike Brey]] considered adding Harangody to the starting lineup, but Harangody hesitated, Steak and Shake still prevalent in his stomach, and Brey decided to wait until Big East play. Harangody would go on to start the team's final 16 games. Harangody went on to average 11.2 points and 6.2 rebounds that season, and was named to the Big East All-Rookie first team. However, conditioning proved to be a problem for him that season; he gained weight during the season (not typical for college athletes), and he played more than 30 minutes only once as a freshman. His conditioning caught up with him in the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. He played only 17 minutes in Notre Dame's first-round loss to [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]], and finished with 4 points and one rebound. About that game, he would later remember that "It was hard to get up and down the court. I hit that wall and there was nothing I could do to get out of it. I never wanted to feel like that again." He then had dinner with his parents shortly after the game, an event which his father clearly remembered in an interview the following season: "On the spot, he says, 'I've got to do something.' He rededicated himself from the minute they lost that game." ===Sophomore season=== {{seealso|2007-08 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team}} His rededication began with a change in diet; he and the team's trainer worked on a nutrition program that limited his intake of fried foods and carbohydrates. Harangody also increased the intensity of his workout regimen, in both cardiovascular work and weight training. The work paid off in his sophomore season; his body fat content dropped from 14% at the end of his freshman season to 8% by the end of the 2007–08 season. Harangody also took more of a leadership role on the team, notably berating several of the team's freshmen for giggling in the locker room after a January 19, 2008 loss to [[2007-08 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]]. Harangody ended the season averaging 20.4 points and 10.6 rebounds,{{cite web|url= http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2007-2008/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND |title=2007–08 Notre Dame Men's Basketball: Notre Dame Season Box Score |publisher=University of Notre Dame Athletic Department |accessdate=2008-10-13}} which made him the Big East's leading scorer and second-leading rebounder.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.org/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2007-2008/CONFLDRS.HTM#conf.wki |title=2007–08 BIG EAST Conference Individual Basketball Statistics |publisher=Big East Conference |date=2008-03-30 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} In contrast to his early doubts about his ability to play in the Big East, he had even better numbers in Big East play, with averages of 23.3 points and 11.3 rebounds, which led the conference in both categories.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.org/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2007-2008/CONFONLY.HTM#conf.wki |title=2007–08 BIG EAST Conference Individual Basketball Statistics (Conference games only) |publisher=Big East Conference |date=2008-03-30 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} This also made him one of only five players in the previous decade to average 22 points and 11 rebounds in conference play for a [[BCS conference]] team. His scoring and leadership led the Irish to a 14–4 conference record and 24–7 regular season record. The Irish also became the first team in Big East men's basketball history to go unbeaten at home in conference play in consecutive seasons.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280650087|title=Irish become first Big East team to go undefeated at home two straight seasons|author=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=''ESPN.com''|date=2008-03-05|accessdate=2008-10-13}} Although the Irish lost in the first round of the Big East tournament to [[Marquette Golden Eagles|Marquette]],{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280730087|title=McNeal's career-high 28 carry Marquette to Big East semis|author=Associated Press| publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2008-03-13|accessdate=2008-10-13}} Notre Dame earned their second straight [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] bid as a #5 seed. The Irish beat [[2007-08 George Mason Patriots men's basketball team|George Mason]] in the first round and went out in the second to [[2007-08 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]]. After the season, Harangody was named the conference [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]], and was also named to the 1st Team All Big East squad.{{cite news|url=http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=1409119|title=2008 All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Teams Announced|publisher=Big East Conference|date=2008-03-10|accessdate=2008-10-13}} He was named to the [[Associated Press]]' [[All-America]] Second Team on March 31, 2008. ===Junior season=== Harangody never considered declaring for the [[2008 NBA Draft]]. With Harangody and fellow All-Big East first-teamer [[Kyle McAlarney]] leading an experienced team, the Irish were expected to make a deep run in the 2009 NCAA Tournament, with [[Dick Vitale]] naming the Irish #6 in his preseason rankings{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/dickvitale/news/story?id=3544438 |title=Dickie V's Preseason Top 40 |first=Dick |last=Vitale |authorlink=Dick Vitale |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2008-09-08 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} and [[Andy Katz]] placing the Irish in a "next tier" of teams that he effectively ranked from 8th to 16th.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?id=3640708 |title= Tar Heels on top as season sets to begin |first=Andy |last=Katz |authorlink=Andy Katz |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2008-10-13 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} However, Notre Dame had to deal with a possible threat to Harangody's college eligibility during the 2008 offseason. A [[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]] company, Cellular Services Worldwide, had obtained [[public domain]] photos of Harangody and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Irish]] [[quarterback]] [[Jimmy Clausen]] and used them in an advertisement on a Notre Dame fan site on the Web. Such a use of images of players is a violation of NCAA rules. The school immediately issued a [[cease and desist]] letter to the company, which satisfied NCAA requirements and ensured the players' eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://myespn.go.com/blogs/others/0-0-48/Morning-Coffee--Notre-Dame-says-cease-and-desist.html |title=Morning Coffee: Cease and Desist |first=Graham |last=Watson |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2008-07-23 |accessdate=2008-10-13}} The Fighting Irish finished a disappointing 21–15, losing in the Final Four of the NIT to Penn State after climbing as high as #7 in the polls during the season. ==See also== * [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]] *[[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball players with 2000 points and 1000 rebounds]] ==Notes and references== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harangody_luke00.html Notre Dame player profile] *[http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=31678 ESPN player profile] {{2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Harangody, Luke}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Illinois]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indiana]] [[Category:Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Decatur, Illinois]] [[Category:People from Lake County, Indiana]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]]
